_doc: Part-b GATE CRITERION #6 (Relay owns this fixture, Forge ships the test, Atlas co-reviews under item-4): locks the REAL device push round-trip that #96 does NOT cover. The deploy's cert-bound apnsSend (NO impl in this repo) wraps the BARE buildDialPayload (dial-payload-v1.json cases[*].payload) in the APNs envelope with the dial fields at TOP LEVEL alongside `aps` -> PKPushPayload.dictionaryPayload = { aps:{...}, v, id, kind, ...bare dial fields }. The app's SentiCallKit decode() and DialReceive.receive read those fields at the TOP LEVEL (aps is an unknown key -> ignored by DialPayloadV1's synthesized Decodable). This fixture owns the ENVELOPE CONTRACT ONLY -- it deliberately carries NO dial-field values, so it can never drift from the KAV (those values are single-sourced from #96's dial-payload-v1.json). The bare (no-envelope) shape is already #96-locked; this adds the enveloped-positive + wrong-nesting-negative + throw-guard coverage.

derivation.positive: for each case C in sourceCases.cases: dict = { "aps": apsEnvelope, ...C.payload } (dial fields spread at TOP LEVEL). JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: dict) -> DialReceive.receive MUST yield dialId == C.payload.id AND state == (C.payload.fetch === true ? needsHydration : renderable). Covers all 6 KAV cases: write-kinds + lean_overflow (fetch=true -> needsHydration), rich_info (fetch=false -> renderable).
derivation.negative: for a sample case C and each K in wrongPlacementKeys: dict = { "aps": apsEnvelope, [K]: C.payload } (DTO NESTED, not top-level). DialReceive.receive MUST yield .rejected -- top-level v/id are absent so decode fails. This is the whole point: a naive apnsSend that nests the DTO under the field it is literally named (`payload`) would silently .reject EVERY ring in production, and only this test catches it.
derivation.throwGuard: a non-JSON-serializable dictionaryPayload -> the receive-hook's `JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject(dict), let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(...)` guard (Warden criterion #5b) MUST skip received()/store .rejected WITHOUT crashing, and STILL ring via decode() for display (a garbage push declines on answer, never hydrates/posts).

deployContract: The TOP-LEVEL placement above is enforced by the deploy's apnsSend (cert-bound, injected via app.mjs deps.apnsSend -- NOT testable from this repo). It is pinned as a documented assumption at the /dial dispatch seam (dial-registry.mjs apnsSend callsite + app.mjs deps.apnsSend JSDoc). This fixture locks OUR side (the decode round-trip); the deploy side stays a contract to honor when Carter wires the VoIP cert.
